mutation_transcript_uniprot_map.name: mutation_transcript_uniprot_map
mutation_transcript_uniprot_map.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.ensembl_transcript_id AS ensembl_transcript_id,
  mp.peptide_id AS peptide_id,
  mp.uniprotkb_ac AS uniprotkb_ac,
  mu.uniprotkb_canonical_ac AS uniprotkb_canonical_ac
FROM
  -- base mutation row-level view providing ensembl_transcript_id per mutation
  disease_mutation_row_level m
  -- left join to mapping table that maps ensembl_transcript_id -> peptide/uniprot accession(s)
  LEFT JOIN map_protein_disease_mutation mp
    ON mp.ensembl_transcript_id = m.ensembl_transcript_id
  -- left join to canonical mapping (may not exist for all uniprot accessions)
  LEFT JOIN map_uniprot_canonical_id mu
    ON mu.uniprotkb_ac = mp.uniprotkb_ac
mutation_transcript_uniprot_map.description: Denormalized mapping of disease mutation transcript identifiers to peptide/protein identifiers (Uniprot) and canonical Uniprot canonical accession when available. Useful for joining mutation records to protein-level annotations.

fda_test_full_details.name: fda_test_full_details
fda_test_full_details.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.test_submission AS test_submission,
  t.test_trade_name AS test_trade_name,
  t.test_manufacturer AS test_manufacturer,
  t.biomarker_origin AS biomarker_origin,
  t.test_approval_status AS test_approval_status,
  t.test_number_genes AS test_number_genes,
  -- aggregate distinct biomarker_drug values for this test_submission into a comma-separated string
  CASE
    WHEN bd.biomarker_drugs IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE bd.biomarker_drugs
  END AS biomarker_drugs,
  -- aggregate distinct ncit_biomarker values for this test_submission into a comma-separated string
  CASE
    WHEN bn.ncit_biomarkers IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE bn.ncit_biomarkers
  END AS ncit_biomarkers
FROM
  biomarker_fda_test t
  -- left join aggregated drugs per test_submission
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
      biomarker_fda_id AS test_submission,
      string_agg(DISTINCT biomarker_drug, ',' ORDER BY biomarker_drug) AS biomarker_drugs
    FROM biomarker_fda_drug
    GROUP BY biomarker_fda_id
  ) bd ON bd.test_submission = t.test_submission
  -- left join aggregated ncit terms per test_submission
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
      biomarker_fda_id AS test_submission,
      string_agg(DISTINCT ncit_biomarker, ',' ORDER BY ncit_biomarker) AS ncit_biomarkers
    FROM biomarker_fda_ncit_term
    GROUP BY biomarker_fda_id
  ) bn ON bn.test_submission = t.test_submission
fda_test_full_details.description: Denormalized FDA test details joined to FDA drug and NCIT term tables where available, one row per test_submission (test primary key). Useful for queries that need wide test context and related drug/term values.

  SELECT

  ON dm_counts.disease_id = d.id

biomarker_fda_test_summary_28.name: biomarker_fda_test_summary_28

biomarker_type_canonical.name: biomarker_type_canonical
biomarker_type_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  biomarker_type,
  -- canonical normalized form: trimmed, lowercased, collapse internal whitespace to single space
  regexp_replace(lower(trim(biomarker_type)), '\s+', ' ', 'g') AS biomarker_type_normalized,
  biomarker_title,
  qa_state,
  phase
FROM biomarker_edrn
biomarker_type_canonical.description: Normalized biomarker type and related classification fields for biomarkers that can be joined to multiple biomarker sources. Canonicalizes biomarker_type to a trimmed form to ease comparisons and downstream filtering.

biomarker_edrn_anatomy_phase_overview.name: biomarker_edrn_anatomy_phase_overview
biomarker_edrn_anatomy_phase_overview.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- normalized biomarker type (lifted literal: treat NULL as 'unknown')
  COALESCE(b.uberon_anatomical_id, '') AS uberon_anatomical_id,
  COALESCE(b.biomarker_type, '') AS biomarker_type_normalized,
  COALESCE(b.phase, '') AS phase,
  COUNT(*)::bigint AS biomarker_count
FROM biomarker_edrn b
-- exclude rows that have neither type nor anatomy nor phase if desired by filters can be applied outside the view
GROUP BY
  COALESCE(b.biomarker_type, ''),
  COALESCE(b.uberon_anatomical_id, ''),
  COALESCE(b.phase, '')
ORDER BY
  COALESCE(b.biomarker_type, ''),
  COALESCE(b.uberon_anatomical_id, ''),
  COALESCE(b.phase, '')
biomarker_edrn_anatomy_phase_overview.description: Aggregate counts of EDRN biomarkers by biomarker_type_normalized, uberon_anatomical_id, and phase to support summarization and faceted filters.

biomarker_title_canonicalized.name: biomarker_title_canonicalized
biomarker_title_canonicalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id,
  b.biomarker_title,
  -- canonicalization: coalesce empty strings to NULL, trim whitespace,
  -- collapse internal whitespace to single space, lower-case for matching,
  -- but keep original case for display in biomarker_title column.
  NULLIF(
    regexp_replace(
      trim(b.biomarker_title),
      '\s+',
      ' ',
      'g'
    ),
    ''
  ) AS biomarker_title,
  -- canonical_biomarker_title lifted literal: use lower-case canonical form without punctuation.
  NULLIF(
    regexp_replace(
      regexp_replace(
        lower(regexp_replace(trim(b.biomarker_title), '\s+', ' ', 'g')),
        '[^\w\s]', '', 'g'
      ),
      '\s+',
      ' ',
      'g'
    ),
    ''
  ) AS canonical_biomarker_title
FROM biomarker_edrn b
biomarker_title_canonicalized.description: Normalized projection of biomarker_edrn titles: trims/cleans NULLs and exposes a canonical_title for display and matching.

differential_expression_labeled.name: differential_expression_labeled
differential_expression_labeled.body_sql:

  de.doid,

differential_expression_labeled.description: Rows from differential_expression with DOID preserved; one row per gene_symbol + doid observation, exposing differential expression metrics and identifiers for joining to disease.

healthy_expression_by_uberon.name: healthy_expression_by_uberon
healthy_expression_by_uberon.body_sql:
SELECT
  he.ensembl_gene_id,
  he.uberon_anatomical_id,
  he.expression_level_gene_relative,
  he.expression_score,
  he.expression_rank_score
FROM healthy_expression he
WHERE he.ensembl_gene_id IS NOT NULL
  AND he.uberon_anatomical_id IS NOT NULL
  -- liftable literal: minimum required quality for inclusion
  AND (he.call_quality IS NULL OR he.call_quality IN ('present','high','good'))
healthy_expression_by_uberon.description: Healthy tissue expression observations keyed by ensembl_gene_id and uberon_anatomical_id; includes expression level metrics and scores for mapping to anatomical entities or cancer_tissue.

ensembl_to_symbol.name: ensembl_to_symbol
ensembl_to_symbol.body_sql:
SELECT
  x.ensembl_gene_id,
  -- prefer the most common/canonical gene_symbol per species in xref_gene_ensembl
  -- lift literal: tie-breaker ordering by gene_symbol ascending
  (   SELECT gene_symbol
      FROM xref_gene_ensembl x2
      WHERE x2.ensembl_gene_id = x.ensembl_gene_id
      ORDER BY gene_symbol NULLS LAST
      LIMIT 1
  ) AS gene_symbol
FROM (
  -- distinct ensembl_gene_id values present in xref_gene_ensembl
  SELECT DISTINCT ensembl_gene_id
  FROM xref_gene_ensembl
  WHERE ensembl_gene_id IS NOT NULL
) x
ensembl_to_symbol.description: Mapping from ensembl_gene_id to canonical gene_symbol for species covered in xref_gene_ensembl; one row per ensembl_gene_id.

disease_row.name: disease_row

biomarker_to_disease_cohort.name: biomarker_to_disease_cohort
biomarker_to_disease_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS biomarker_id,
  b.gene_symbol,
  b.biomarker_description,
  d.id::bigint AS disease_id,
  d.name AS disease_name,
  -- match_type: prefer explicit links (fda/test origin), then mention-based fallback
  CASE
    WHEN bf.test_submission IS NOT NULL THEN 'fda_test_association'
    WHEN be.id IS NOT NULL THEN 'edrn_association'
    WHEN lower(b.gene_symbol) = lower(d.name) THEN 'gene_equals_disease_name'
    WHEN b.gene_symbol IS NOT NULL AND d.name IS NOT NULL AND position(lower(d.name) IN lower(b.gene_symbol)) > 0 THEN 'gene_mentions_disease'
    WHEN b.biomarker_description IS NOT NULL AND d.name IS NOT NULL AND position(lower(d.name) IN lower(b.biomarker_description)) > 0 THEN 'description_mentions_disease'
    ELSE 'unknown'
  END AS match_type
FROM biomarker b
-- direct FDA test associations via biomarker_fda -> biomarker_fda_test (if present)
LEFT JOIN biomarker_fda bfda ON bfda.id = b.id
LEFT JOIN biomarker_fda_test bf ON bf.test_trade_name = bfda.test_trade_name AND bf.test_submission = bfda.test_submission
-- EDRN biomarker linking by id field if present (biomarker_edrn.id may match biomarker.id)
LEFT JOIN biomarker_edrn be ON be.id = b.id
-- diseases: include all diseases to allow mention-based matching; prefer joining by DOID where available from fda test (doid) or edrn. Use COALESCE to surface a candidate disease when explicit id exists.
LEFT JOIN disease d ON
  (
    -- if FDA test provided a doid link
    (bf.doid IS NOT NULL AND d.id = bf.doid)
    -- or if EDRN provided an uberon_anatomical_id we cannot map to disease here, so no join
    -- fallback: attempt textual matching between biomarker fields and disease name (case-insensitive)
    OR (bf.doid IS NULL AND be.id IS NULL AND (
         (b.gene_symbol IS NOT NULL AND position(lower(d.name) IN lower(b.gene_symbol)) > 0)
         OR (b.biomarker_description IS NOT NULL AND position(lower(d.name) IN lower(b.biomarker_description)) > 0)
         OR (b.gene_symbol IS NOT NULL AND lower(b.gene_symbol) = lower(d.name))
       ))
  )
WHERE
  -- keep only biomarkers (grain is one row per biomarker). When multiple disease matches exist for same biomarker this will duplicate biomarker rows;
  -- if strict one-row-per-biomarker is required, additional aggregation outside this view should be used. Here include any explicit or mention-based matches.
  (
    bf.test_submission IS NOT NULL
    OR be.id IS NOT NULL
    OR (
      (b.gene_symbol IS NOT NULL AND EXISTS (
         SELECT 1 FROM disease d2 WHERE position(lower(d2.name) IN lower(b.gene_symbol)) > 0 OR lower(d2.name) = lower(b.gene_symbol)
      ))
    )
    OR (
      (b.biomarker_description IS NOT NULL AND EXISTS (
         SELECT 1 FROM disease d3 WHERE position(lower(d3.name) IN lower(b.biomarker_description)) > 0
      ))
    )
  )
biomarker_to_disease_cohort.description: Denormalized candidate links between biomarkers and diseases. This view attempts to expose direct links where present in the schema (if there are linking tables in other chunks they can be added). As a fallback it includes biomarkers whose gene_symbol or biomarker_description mention the disease name (case-insensitive). Not all links may be present in this schema chunk; this view is a reusable join/cohort for biomarker-by-disease queries.

disease_mutation_with_articles_and_predi.name: disease_mutation_with_articles_and_predictions
disease_mutation_with_articles_and_predi.body_sql:
SELECT

  dm.ref_aa,

  dm.mutation_freq,
  dm.data_source,
  dm.doid,
  dma.pmid,
  dmp.id AS "disease_mutation_impact_prediction.id",
  dmp.site_prediction AS "disease_mutation_impact_prediction.site_prediction",
  dmp.probability AS "disease_mutation_impact_prediction.probability",
  dmp.tool AS "disease_mutation_impact_prediction.tool"
FROM

  -- left join to articles: preserve rows only when there is an article; cross with predictions below to get multiplicity
  LEFT JOIN disease_mutation_article AS dma
    ON dma.disease_mutation_id = dm.id
  -- left join to predictions: preserve predictions when present; will produce one row per (dm.id x pmid x prediction)
  LEFT JOIN disease_mutation_impact_prediction AS dmp
    ON dmp.disease_mutation_id = dm.id
WHERE
  -- lift nothing here; include all rows. Use no filter so literals are not embedded.
  TRUE

differential_expression_canonical.name: differential_expression_canonical
differential_expression_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  de.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol,
  de.doid AS doid,
  de.log2fc AS log2fc,
  de.adjpvalue AS adjpvalue,
  -- Canonicalize expression_change_direction:
  -- lift literal values OUT so view consumers can substitute if desired
  -- 'up_value' -> represents textual up-regulation indicator in source
  -- 'down_value' -> represents textual down-regulation indicator in source
  -- 'nochange_value' -> represents textual no-change indicator in source
  CASE
    WHEN de.expression_change_direction = 'up_value' THEN 'up'
    WHEN de.expression_change_direction = 'down_value' THEN 'down'
    WHEN de.expression_change_direction = 'nochange_value' THEN 'no_change'
    ELSE lower(coalesce(de.expression_change_direction, 'unknown'))
  END AS expression_change_direction,
  -- Canonicalize statistical_significance:
  -- lift literal 'significant_value' to denote source's significant marker
  CASE
    WHEN de.statistical_significance = 'significant_value' THEN 'significant'
    WHEN de.statistical_significance = 'not_significant_value' THEN 'not_significant'
    ELSE lower(coalesce(de.statistical_significance, 'unknown'))
  END AS statistical_significance
FROM
  differential_expression de
differential_expression_canonical.description: Normalized/projection view of differential_expression rows with canonicalized expression direction, canonical significance flag, and kept raw statistical measures. One row per differential_expression record.

  lower(

differential_expression_significance_fla.name: differential_expression_significance_flags
differential_expression_significance_fla.body_sql:
SELECT
  de.gene_symbol,

  de.statistical_significance,
  -- canonical boolean flag: true when statistical_significance text denotes significance
  -- Lift literal values out: significant_indicators list
  (de.statistical_significance IS NOT NULL
   AND lower(trim(de.statistical_significance)) IN (lower('significant'), lower('yes'), lower('true'), lower('s'), lower('sig'), lower('statistically significant'))
  ) AS is_significant,
  de.log2fc,
  de.pvalue,
  de.adjpvalue,
  de.subjects_total
FROM

FROM

LEFT JOIN
  disease dis
    ON d.doid = dis.id
WHERE
  -- liftable literal: minimum significance to include; change as needed
  d.adjpvalue IS NOT NULL
  AND d.adjpvalue < 0.05
gene_to_disease_significant_expr.description: Denormalized rows linking differential expression measurements to disease names for quick filtering of significant expression results per gene. One row per gene_symbol x doid with disease metadata included.

biomarker_basic.name: biomarker_basic
biomarker_basic.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS id,
  b.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol,
  b.biomarker_description AS biomarker_description,
  b.biomarker_id AS biomarker_id,
  b.test_is_a_panel AS test_is_a_panel
FROM biomarker b
biomarker_basic.description: One-row-per-biomarker canonical projection exposing primary identifiers, display name and descriptive text (keeps NULLs). Suitable as the base relation for listing or filtering biomarkers.
counter_examples: Get the biomarker gene symbol and biomarker description for disease with name 'breast cancer'

biomarker_aliases_70.name: biomarker_aliases_70
biomarker_aliases_70.description: All aliases for biomarkers, one row per alias entry. Useful to join or search alternate names for biomarkers.

biomarker_articles_71.name: biomarker_articles_71
biomarker_articles_71.body_sql:
SELECT
  bma.biomarker_internal_id AS biomarker_internal_id,
  bma.pmid AS pmid
FROM
  biomarker_article bma
biomarker_articles_71.description: Mapping of biomarkers to literature PMIDs, one row per biomarker-article association. Useful to attach evidence or count publications per biomarker.

biomarker_aliass_flat.name: biomarker_aliass_flat
biomarker_aliass_flat.body_sql:
SELECT
  ba.biomarker_internal_id,
  ba.alias
FROM
  biomarker_alias ba
biomarker_aliass_flat.description: One row per biomarker alias linking biomarker id to each alias (useful for searches that match alternate names).

biomarker_with_fda_test_summary.name: biomarker_with_fda_test_summary
biomarker_with_fda_test_summary.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS biomarker_id,
  b.gene_symbol,
  b.biomarker_description,
  t.test_submission,
  t.test_trade_name,
  t.test_manufacturer,
  t.test_approval_status
FROM biomarker AS b
LEFT JOIN biomarker_fda AS bf ON bf.id = b.id
LEFT JOIN biomarker_fda_test AS t ON t.test_submission = bf.test_submission
biomarker_with_fda_test_summary.description: Denormalized biomarker-to-FDA-test relation: one row per biomarker.id paired with FDA test info when available (useful to filter biomarkers by FDA test attributes).

fda_test_use_rows.name: fda_test_use_rows
fda_test_use_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  bfu.id::bigint AS id,
  bfu.test_trade_name,
  bfu.test_submission,
  bfu.approved_indication,
  bfu.actual_use
FROM biomarker_fda_test_use bfu
fda_test_use_rows.description: Row-level cohort of FDA test use records (one row per biomarker_fda_test_use record) with key identifiers and use/application attributes.

fda_test_trade_names_dedup.name: fda_test_trade_names_dedup
fda_test_trade_names_dedup.body_sql:
SELECT
  test_trade_name,
  -- lift literal: choose representative as the first-seen test_submission (lowest sort order)
  -- representative_test_submission is the MIN(test_submission) per test_trade_name to be deterministic
  MIN(test_submission) AS representative_test_submission
FROM
  fda_test_full_details
GROUP BY
  test_trade_name
fda_test_trade_names_dedup.description: Distinct FDA test trade names deduplicated (one row per test_trade_name) using first-seen test_submission as deterministic tie-breaker.

biomarker_row_level_76.name: biomarker_row_level_76
biomarker_row_level_76.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS id,
  b.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol,
  b.biomarker_description AS biomarker_description,
  b.biomarker_id AS biomarker_id,
  b.test_is_a_panel AS test_is_a_panel
FROM biomarker b
biomarker_row_level_76.description: Row-level view exposing biomarker records for general filtering and selection (one row per biomarker).

biomarker_canonical_gene.name: biomarker_canonical_gene
biomarker_canonical_gene.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS id,
  -- canonicalize gene_symbol: treat NULL or empty-string as NULL,
  -- otherwise trim whitespace. Lift literal '' out if needed by callers.
  NULLIF(NULLIF(trim(b.gene_symbol), ''), '') AS gene_symbol
FROM biomarker b
biomarker_canonical_gene.description: Normalized/cleaned biomarker gene information: canonicalize NULL/empty gene symbols and expose gene identifier fields for joining or grouping.

biomarker_with_aliases.name: biomarker_with_aliases
biomarker_with_aliases.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS biomarker_id,
  b.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol,
  ba.alias AS alias
FROM biomarker b
LEFT JOIN biomarker_alias ba
  ON ba.biomarker_internal_id = b.id
biomarker_with_aliases.description: Denormalized relation joining biomarkers to their aliases so queries can match either official gene_symbol or alias strings.

biomarker_edrn_with_anatomy_79.name: biomarker_edrn_with_anatomy_79
biomarker_edrn_with_anatomy_79.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS id,
  b.qa_state AS qa_state,
  b.biomarker_title AS biomarker_title,
  b.biomarker_type AS biomarker_type,
  b.uberon_anatomical_id AS uberon_anatomical_id,
  b.phase AS phase,
  a.name AS "anatomical_entity.name",
  a.description AS "anatomical_entity.description"
FROM biomarker_edrn b
LEFT JOIN anatomical_entity a
  ON b.uberon_anatomical_id = a.id
biomarker_edrn_with_anatomy_79.description: Denormalized view joining biomarker_edrn to anatomical_entity via uberon_anatomical_id to expose the anatomical name/description alongside the EDRN biomarker row. One row per biomarker_edrn.id (biomarker-centric).

biomarker_edrn_with_anatomy_80.name: biomarker_edrn_with_anatomy_80
biomarker_edrn_with_anatomy_80.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS id,
  b.biomarker_title AS biomarker_title,
  b.biomarker_type AS biomarker_type,
  b.phase AS phase,
  b.uberon_anatomical_id AS uberon_anatomical_id,
  a.name AS "anatomical_entity.name AS anatomical_name"
FROM
  biomarker_edrn b
LEFT JOIN
  anatomical_entity a
    ON b.uberon_anatomical_id = a.id
biomarker_edrn_with_anatomy_80.description: Denormalized biomarker_edrn rows joined to anatomical_entity by uberon_anatomical_id to provide human-readable anatomical names along with biomarker metadata. One row per biomarker_edrn.id; useful for queries that filter by anatomical site or display the anatomical name next to biomarker titles.

biomarker_disease_link_candidates.name: biomarker_disease_link_candidates
biomarker_disease_link_candidates.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS biomarker_id,
  dm.doid AS disease_id,
  'disease_mutation->map_protein_disease_mutation->biomarker (uniprot match)' AS linking_path,
  'medium' AS link_strength_hint
FROM disease_mutation dm
JOIN map_protein_disease_mutation mpdm
  ON dm.ensembl_transcript_id = mpdm.ensembl_transcript_id
JOIN biomarker b
  ON mpdm.uniprotkb_ac = b.biomarker_id
UNION
SELECT
  b.id AS biomarker_id,
  dm.doid AS disease_id,
  'disease_mutation->map_protein_disease_mutation->biomarker (ensembl transcript match)' AS linking_path,
  'medium' AS link_strength_hint
FROM disease_mutation dm
JOIN map_protein_disease_mutation mpdm
  ON dm.ensembl_transcript_id = mpdm.ensembl_transcript_id
JOIN biomarker b
  ON mpdm.ensembl_transcript_id = b.biomarker_id
UNION
SELECT
  b.id AS biomarker_id,
  dm.doid AS disease_id,
  'disease_mutation->disease_mutation_tissue->cancer_tissue->biomarker_fda_test (tissue/DOID mapping)' AS linking_path,
  'low' AS link_strength_hint
FROM disease_mutation dm
JOIN disease_mutation_tissue dmt
  ON dm.id = dmt.disease_mutation_id
JOIN cancer_tissue ct
  ON dmt.uberon_anatomical_id = ct.uberon_anatomical_id
JOIN biomarker_fda_test bft
  ON ct.doid = bft.doid
JOIN biomarker_fda bfd
  ON bft.test_submission = bfd.test_submission
JOIN biomarker b
  ON bfd.id = b.id
UNION
SELECT
  b.id AS biomarker_id,
  dm.doid AS disease_id,
  'disease_mutation->map_protein_disease_mutation->map_uniprot_canonical_id->biomarker (canonical uniprot match)' AS linking_path,
  'medium' AS link_strength_hint
FROM disease_mutation dm
JOIN map_protein_disease_mutation mpdm
  ON dm.ensembl_transcript_id = mpdm.ensembl_transcript_id
JOIN map_uniprot_canonical_id muc
  ON mpdm.uniprotkb_ac = muc.uniprotkb_ac
JOIN biomarker b
  ON muc.uniprotkb_canonical_ac = b.biomarker_id
UNION
SELECT
  b.id AS biomarker_id,
  d.id AS disease_id,
  'biomarker.gene_symbol->xref_gene_ensembl->differential_expression->disease (expression link)' AS linking_path,
  'low' AS link_strength_hint
FROM biomarker b
JOIN xref_gene_ensembl xe
  ON b.gene_symbol = xe.gene_symbol
JOIN differential_expression de
  ON xe.ensembl_gene_id = de.gene_symbol
JOIN disease d
  ON de.doid = d.id
WHERE de.statistical_significance = 'significant'
biomarker_disease_link_candidates.description: Candidate link rows between biomarkers and diseases using available mapping tables in the schema chunk. This brings together biomarkers and disease ids when a mapping exists through disease_mutation -> map_protein_disease_mutation -> biomarker or other plausible paths. It is intentionally inclusive (UNION) so downstream queries can filter by stronger links if desired.

edrn_biomarker_overview.name: edrn_biomarker_overview
edrn_biomarker_overview.body_sql:
SELECT
  be.id,
  be.biomarker_title,
  be.biomarker_type,
  be.phase,
  be.uberon_anatomical_id
FROM
  biomarker_edrn be
edrn_biomarker_overview.description: Denormalized overview of EDRN biomarkers combining id, title, type, phase, and anatomical mapping (uberon_anatomical_id). One row per biomarker_edrn to support filtering/grouping by phase, type, or anatomical site.

biomarker_phase_counts_per_type.name: biomarker_phase_counts_per_type
biomarker_phase_counts_per_type.body_sql:
SELECT
  biomarker_edrn.phase                                 AS phase,
  biomarker_edrn.biomarker_type                        AS biomarker_type,
  COUNT(*)                                             AS biomarker_count
FROM
  biomarker_edrn
GROUP BY
  biomarker_edrn.phase,
  biomarker_edrn.biomarker_type
biomarker_phase_counts_per_type.description: Aggregate counts of biomarker_edrn records by phase and biomarker_type. One row per (phase, biomarker_type). Useful for quickly answering distribution questions across phases and types; does not pre-aggregate to a single scalar so it remains reusable.

differential_expression_with_disease_84.name: differential_expression_with_disease_84
differential_expression_with_disease_84.body_sql:
SELECT
  de.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol,
  de.doid AS doid,
  de.pvalue AS pvalue,
  de.log2fc AS log2fc,
  de.adjpvalue AS adjpvalue,
  de.statistical_significance AS statistical_significance,
  de.expression_change_direction AS expression_change_direction,
  de.subjects_total AS subjects_total,
  d.name AS disease_name
FROM
  differential_expression de
LEFT JOIN
  disease d
ON
  de.doid = d.id
differential_expression_with_disease_84.description: Denormalized view joining differential_expression to disease so queries can directly filter by disease.name while retaining all differential expression metrics.
